pre_mortem: It's Monday and both legs lost because New England led 17-0 after a short field, Miami went pass-heavy into the blitz, and Gordon was stuck near 8 carries and the mid-30s while Willis locked onto Washington and the failed deep shots to Coleman and Bell. Dulcich saw two targets for about 11 yards because NE's linebackers sat on the hooks once the run was gone, and the 61.5 and 28.5 both stood. The other way this dies is the reverse: Gordon goes for 110 in a 13-10 rock fight and Dulcich never gets a target because Willis hands it off 30 times. That counter-case is real enough to keep both at lean, not strong, and to forbid pairing Gordon's over with a Miami pass-volume story that needs a blowout.
slip_story: One story only: Miami stays competitive in a low-total outdoor grind, so the offense is Gordon on the ground plus Dulcich as the middle checkdown against NE's 39% blitz and 11.74 middle YPA. Those two win together in a one-score game. Do not stack them with NE shootout overs (Douglas/Brown air yards) or with a Miami total that requires a shutout. Henry over 45.5 is the NE-side cousin of the same middle-bleed idea but is a different team's script and was left off to keep the slip to one story and two legs.
